focus: Ponytail verification and measurement mechanisms vs sk-code verification doctrine and test surfaces
noveltyJustification: 5 fully new mechanisms (grader self-test, measurement-vs-gate separation with declared instrument limits, published-number hygiene, correctness counterweight, reproducibility contract), 1 lost-capability finding (deterministic routing measurement retired while its corpus and design remain), 2 already-adopted (persisted-evidence no-mocks contract stronger, host-quirk coverage).
keyQuestions: Which Ponytail verification and test-suite mechanisms are absent, adopted, or rejected in sk-code's verification doctrine and test surfaces?
answeredQuestions: Which Ponytail verification and test-suite mechanisms are absent, adopted, or rejected in sk-code's verification doctrine and test surfaces?
ruledOut: Importing Ponytail's headline restraint percentages as sk-code targets or gates (benchmark-only ruling stands)
Treating the frozen benchmark index as current capability (it cannot start a run)

graphEvents.label: sk-code frozen benchmark index and playbook

label: Ponytail unit-tests its own graders: behavior.test.js feeds behavior-present and behavior-absent outputs through each probe checker and asserts the verdict, with the stated purpose that this is what makes the eval trustworthy; sk-code has no located self-test of its routing-verdict mechanism. Classification: NEW.

Ponytail declares measurement-only versus gating metrics inside the harness (loc.js measurement-only; correctness.js a gate because a wrong answer is wrong however few lines produced it) and names each instrument's weak checks (React and FastAPI checks structural-only); sk-code's frozen index has no correctness arm and no per-check strength statement. Classification: NEW.

Ponytail annotates its own headline number with the instrument bias, credits the external critic who caught it, and re-measures with a better method (single-shot prose-counting win replaced by an agentic session benchmark); combined with the gain command's ban on per-repo savings numbers this is a complete published-number hygiene practice absent from sk-code's frozen verdicts. Classification: NEW.

The agentic benchmark reports hidden checks passed beside every restraint measure (-53% LOC, -45% tokens, -26% cost, -41% time, 97% vs 96% checks) plus the risky-logic test rate (98% vs 68%); the separable idea is the counterweight column so no restraint win can be read alone. Classification: NEW (prior research's benchmark-only ruling stands).

sk-code's routing-quality measurement path is retired and frozen: the Lane C harness, runner, scoring contract and /deep:skill-benchmark command were removed and no new run can start, yet the document records that the deterministic offline router mode was the CI gate over the 28-scenario playbook corpus with verdicts PASS 84/100 and live CONDITIONAL 71/100. The corpus and replay design still exist, so reinstating a deterministic router gate is the concrete restoration. Classification: LOST.

Ponytail's benchmark artifact carries its own reproducibility contract: reproduce commands, the promptfoo Node engine constraint with a check instruction, the --env-file directory gotcha, and stated run counts and aggregation; sk-code's frozen index can state verdicts but no reproduce path because the runner is gone. Classification: NEW.

sk-code's live verification path requires persisted PASS/FAIL/SKIP outcomes and reasons and forbids substitutes (no mocks, no stubs, no unautomatable verdicts; PASS, PARTIAL, FAIL, SKIP only), a stronger contract than Ponytail's aggregate-only reporting. Classification: ALREADY-ADOPTED (stronger).

Both systems test host quirks at different layers: Ponytail ships 18 suites including per-host plugin tests plus a Windows stdin/BOM suite; sk-code's .skilled tree holds 177 test files outside sandboxes including per-runtime hook suites. Whether sk-code covers Windows stdin/BOM behavior equivalently was not located and remains unverified, not a claimed gap. Classification: ALREADY-ADOPTED (one sub-question unverified).
